abstract: Tubulin autoregulation is an essential function that controls the concentration of cellular soluble tubulin. This process is mediated by TTC5 which binds the REI/C polypeptide sequence found in all α- and β-TUBULIN proteins. The recent discovery of TTC5 as the primary tubulin autoregulation pathway mediator and the identification of human brain malformations caused by TTC5 variants poses a need for an in vivo system to elucidate the gene-disease relationship. Here, we present an in vivo Ttc5 mouse model that phenocopies many of the human TTC5 clinical presentations. The brain malformations in Ttc5null/null mice are driven by neurogenesis defects, which are in turn caused by perturbations in mitosis. We found that increased γ-TUBULIN levels in Ttc5null/null brains likely facilitate mitotic errors. We posit that the paradigm of tubulin autoregulation should be expanded to include γ-tubulin and that this expansion provides a mechanistic base for tubulin autoregulation brain malformations.
